data.summary: The client approved the design before delivery and the freelancer provided a download link containing the promised vector files, but the client never actually downloaded the master vector package and later raised an unanswered complaint about missing print‑ready assets. data.rationale: The contract explicitly promised master vector source files as part of the Final Asset Package (CONTRACT §3.2). The client approved the design before final delivery (EMAILS E4), satisfying the acceptance test. The freelancer sent a download link that included the master vector zip (EMAILS E6), but delivery logs show the zip was never downloaded (DELIVERY-LOG L5), meaning the client never received the essential files needed for signage. The client’s later contact‑form message and lack of a sign by the opening date demonstrate that the delivered assets are not fit for the advertised purpose (CONTACT-FORM F1, SOCIAL S2). Under the contract’s refund clause, fees are non‑refundable except when the studio fails to deliver the Final Asset Package (CONTRACT §8); the missing master files constitute such a failure. Therefore the chargeback is partially justified. The dispute should be contested for the portion of the fee covering work that was delivered and accepted, while a partial refund of $600.00 compensates for the undelivered master vector files. The freelancer should also promptly provide the missing files and confirm ownership rights to resolve the real complaint.

evidences.notes:
The contract explicitly requires delivery of master vector source files in AI, SVG and EPS formats suitable for print, signage and merchandise as part of the Final Asset Package. [1]

The client gave written approval of the design on June 29, confirming acceptance and requesting the final files. [2]

On July 1 the freelancer emailed the Final Asset Package, including a download link for the master vector zip file. [3]

Delivery logs record zero downloads of the master vector zip, indicating the client never received the essential files. [4]

The client later reported that the sign company could only use screen‑only files and could not produce the storefront sign, confirming the missing master files made the assets unfit for purpose. [5]

The contract’s refund clause states fees are non‑refundable after written approval except when the studio fails to deliver the Final Asset Package. [6]

Because the master vector files were not delivered, the studio failed to provide the Full Asset Package, justifying a partial refund of $600 for the undelivered portion while retaining payment for the work that was accepted. [6][4]

The freelancer will resend the Halden_Master_Vectors_and_Copyright.zip immediately, confirm the client’s download, and issue the $600 partial refund to resolve the issue. [1]

body.note: Immediately resend the Halden_Master_Vectors_and_Copyright.zip via a new download link, confirm with the client that the files are downloaded, and provide written confirmation that the client holds full ownership rights. Issue a partial refund of $600.00 to compensate for the undelivered master vector files.
